addisons-disease: Steroid sick-day rules aren't optional extras. Double the dose when you're sick, and carry the card.
‘Adrenal fatigue’ isn't Addison's. One is a real, testable disease; the other is a supplement aisle.
anaphylaxis: Antihistamines are for hives. Adrenaline is for anaphylaxis. Don't swap the understudy in for the lead.
Lying down with your legs up isn't laziness here. Standing up suddenly can be dangerous.
antibiotics: Green snot is not a prescription. It's just snot doing its job.
Finishing someone else's leftover pills is not a treatment plan. Neither is saving yours for next time.
arsenic: ‘Organic’ rice isn't arsenic-free. Rinsing and cooking in lots of water helps more than the label does.
Victorian wallpaper killed more people than most poisoners. Green was a dangerous colour.
bird-flu: Raw milk from sick cows is not a wellness trend. It's a delivery system.
Your backyard chooks aren't the enemy. Wash your hands after the eggs, not just after the news.
bladder-cancer: Smoking reaches your bladder too. Everything you inhale eventually gets filtered by your kidneys.
A UTI that keeps ‘coming back’ in an older smoker deserves more than another round of antibiotics.
bunions: Pointy shoes: fashionable for an evening, structural damage for life.
Surgery fixes bunions. It does not fix the stilettos that made them.
cadmium: Your phone battery won't poison you. Your cigarettes might.
Detox foot pads don't pull out cadmium. They just go brown when they get damp.
cancer-screening: Feeling fine is exactly when screening works. That's the whole point.
The bowel test kit in your drawer isn't doing anything in there. Poo on the stick.
chronic-kidney-disease: Kidney cleanse teas cleanse your wallet. Your kidneys already do the cleansing for free.
Ibuprofen every day for years is not ‘just a painkiller’ to your kidneys.
chronic-rhinosinusitis: Twelve weeks of a blocked nose isn't a cold that's overstayed. It's a different problem.
Antibiotics rarely fix chronic sinusitis. Rinses and steroid sprays do the heavy lifting.
concussion: Waking someone every hour all night is an old myth. Sleep is fine if they're otherwise okay.
Back to sport the next day isn't tough. It's a gamble with your brain.
covid: ‘Just a cold’ is a diagnosis made by a test, not by hope.
Ivermectin is a brilliant horse dewormer. For COVID, the trials said no.
crohns-disease: Crohn's isn't caused by stress or a bad diet. You didn't eat your way into this.
Smoking makes Crohn's worse. It's one of the few things you can actually change.
cte: Helmets stop skull fractures. They don't stop the brain sloshing inside the skull.
‘He just got his bell rung’ is how a lot of these stories started.
cteph: Being puffed after a clot isn't always deconditioning. Sometimes the clot is still there.
It's one of the few forms of lung blood pressure that surgery can actually cure. Worth finding.
d-mer: It's a hormone dip, not a feeling about your baby. Your brain chemistry is not a parenting review.
Naming it often helps more than anything. It's real, it's physical, and it has a name.
ehlers-danlos-syndrome: ‘Double-jointed’ isn't a diagnosis. Neither is ‘just anxious’.
Being bendy and being in pain all the time are two different things. The second one deserves attention.
eosinophilic-oesophagitis: Food getting stuck isn't ‘eating too fast’ if it happens every week.
It's allergy-related, but a skin-prick test won't find the culprit. A scope and biopsies do.
female-infertility: ‘Just relax and it'll happen’ has never once been a fertility treatment.
Age matters, but it isn't a cliff at 35. It's a slope, and it's different for everyone.
fibroids: Iron tablets for heavy periods treat the result, not the cause. Ask about the cause.
Fibroids are rarely cancer. They're common, they're treatable, and they're not your fault.
flu-and-covid: The flu shot can't give you the flu. Your timing just happened to be bad.
Antibiotics don't touch either virus. Rest, fluids and antivirals for the right people do.
folate: A multivitamin ‘for women’ may not have enough folic acid for pregnancy. Check the dose.
Leafy greens are great. They're just not reliable enough on their own before conception.
gilbert-syndrome: It's a lab quirk, not a liver disease. Your liver is fine; it's just slow at one job.
You don't need a liver detox. You never did.
h-pylori: A breath test, a week of pills, and a lifetime of fewer ulcers. Medicine doesn't get much tidier.
Retest after treatment. Assuming it worked is how ulcers come back.
haemochromatosis: Iron supplements ‘for energy’ are the worst idea here. Get your levels checked first.
Giving blood is the treatment. It's the rare medical plan that also helps a stranger.
heart-failure: Swollen ankles and breathlessness lying flat aren't ‘just getting older’. Get them checked.
Weighing yourself every morning sounds boring. It's one of the best early-warning systems there is.
heavy-metal-testing: Hair tests can find ‘toxins’ in a wig. That should tell you something.
Chelation without real poisoning isn't detox. It can strip out minerals you actually need.
inflammatory-bowel-disease: Bleeding from the bottom is never ‘probably piles’ until someone has looked.
IBD isn't caused by stress or bad food. Stress just makes everything feel worse.
influenza: Real flu flattens you. If you went to work, it probably wasn't flu.
The flu shot changes every year because the virus does. Last year's doesn't cover this year's.
keratoconus: Glasses that never seem quite right might not be the optometrist's fault. It might be the shape of your cornea.
Corneal cross-linking can stop it getting worse. Earlier beats later.
keratosis-pilaris: It's harmless, common and not a hygiene problem. Your skin is just enthusiastic.
Moisturiser with urea or lactic acid beats scrubbing every time.
lactose-intolerance: Hard cheese and yoghurt are low in lactose. Your cheese board can stay.
Lactose intolerance isn't a milk allergy. One gives you gas; the other can stop you breathing.
lead: Old paint plus a sander equals lead dust in the lungs of everyone in the house.
Ayurvedic and imported traditional remedies have tested positive for lead. Natural isn't the same as safe.
leptospirosis: Rats and flood water are a bad combination. Boots on, cuts covered.
It can look like the flu, then turn on your kidneys and liver. Mention the flood water to your doctor.
long-covid: Graded exercise for everyone is out. Pacing to avoid crashes is in.
‘It's all in your head’ isn't a diagnosis. It's an excuse not to look harder.
lupus: It's never lupus, until it is. Then it's the great mimic, and it's been hiding in plain sight.
Sunscreen is a lupus treatment. Seriously. The sun can trigger flares.
male-infertility: About half of fertility problems involve the male side. It's a two-person test.
Laptops on laps, hot tubs and anabolic steroids: one of these is a much bigger problem than the others.
measles: Measles isn't a mild rash. It can wipe your immune system's memory of other infections.
It's so contagious that it can linger in a room for up to two hours after someone leaves.
mercury: Your amalgam fillings aren't poisoning you. Drilling healthy ones out releases more mercury than leaving them.
Skin-lightening creams bought online have been found full of mercury. Read the label, if there is one.
mould: Not every cough is mould. Not every mould is toxic. Not every test is real.
‘Mould illness’ clinics that sell the test, the diagnosis and the cure are a business model, not a diagnosis.
myasthenia-gravis: Droopy eyelids that are worse at night aren't always tiredness. Sometimes they're a clue.
Some common antibiotics can make it worse. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist you have it.
niacin: Niacin raises good cholesterol but didn't prevent heart attacks in big trials. Numbers aren't outcomes.
‘Flush-free’ niacin may not be niacin you can actually absorb. Read the fine print.
ovarian-cysts: Most ovarian cysts are just ovaries doing their monthly job, a little too enthusiastically.
Sudden severe pain on one side is not something to sleep off. That's an emergency.
peptides: ‘Not for human consumption’ is not a loophole. It's a warning.
If the only evidence is a rat study and a podcast, the experiment is you.
pharmacogenomics: Your genes don't pick your antidepressant. They can help rule out a few.
A DNA test from a wellness clinic isn't the same as a medical-grade pharmacogenomic test.
porphyria: Some attacks are triggered by common medicines. Always tell every doctor, every time.
It was once linked to King George III's ‘madness’. Historians still argue about it.
prostate-cancer: A PSA test is a question, not an answer. Talk about it before you do it.
Many men die with prostate cancer, not from it. The trick is knowing which kind you have.
riboflavin: Bright yellow wee after vitamins is your body showing you what it didn't need.
Riboflavin is one of the few supplements with decent evidence for migraine prevention. Ask first.
sarcoidosis: Many cases settle on their own. Watchful waiting is a real treatment plan, not neglect.
It can affect almost any organ, which is why it fools so many doctors.
scleroderma: Cold fingers that go white then blue are Raynaud's. Add tight skin, and it needs a proper look.
Early treatment can protect the lungs. Late diagnosis is the real enemy here.
scombroid: Cooking the fish doesn't destroy the histamine. Neither does freezing it afterwards.
Everyone at the table got hives after the tuna? That's not a family allergy. That's the fish.
sexually-transmitted-infections: No symptoms doesn't mean no infection. Chlamydia is famously quiet.
Getting tested is just maintenance. Like a car service, but for your bits.
sibo: Bloating after a big meal is digestion, not a disease.
Breath tests for SIBO are far from perfect. A positive result isn't always the answer.
smith-magenis-syndrome: The body clock is genuinely reversed in this condition. It's biology, not bad routines.
Melatonin timing matters here more than almost anywhere else. Get specialist advice.
stiff-person-syndrome: Muscles locking when you're startled isn't anxiety. It's a neurological sign.
It's rare, but blood tests for the antibodies exist. Ask if the pattern fits.
thallium: Thallium makes hair fall out two or three weeks after poisoning. That delay is what fools people.
It's colourless, odourless and tasteless, which is exactly why poisoners liked it.
thiamine: Heavy drinkers need thiamine before the sugar drip, not after. Order matters.
After weight-loss surgery, thiamine deficiency can happen fast. Keep taking the vitamins.
tourette-syndrome: Tics often get worse when people stare. Not staring is a genuinely helpful thing you can do.
Many tics improve in the late teens. Tourette's isn't always lifelong at full volume.
travel-vaccines: Some vaccines need weeks to work, or two doses. The day before you fly is too late.
Rabies shots are worth it for long trips. Cute monkeys bite.
ulcerative-colitis: Flares aren't your fault, and they're not just stress. They're inflammation.
Staying on your medicine when you feel well is what keeps you well.
varicose-veins: They're mostly cosmetic. Leg ulcers, bleeding and skin changes are the exceptions that need a look.
Standing jobs don't cause them. They just show off the ones your genes gave you.
vitamin-a: Too much vitamin A in pregnancy can harm the baby. Skip the liver pâté and high-dose supplements.
Carrots won't let you see in the dark. That was wartime propaganda.
vitamin-b6: B6 toxicity is real, and it's usually from supplements you didn't know had B6 in them. Check the labels.
Tingling feet from a vitamin is not ‘the vitamin working’. Stop it and tell your doctor.
vitamin-c: Vitamin C won't stop you catching a cold. It might shave a few hours off one.
Megadoses mostly end up in your urine. Very expensive urine.
vitamin-e: Vitamin E doesn't heal scars faster. Studies found it can make some worse.
More isn't better. High doses can increase bleeding, especially with blood thinners.
